Research the standard feature set of Minecraft server web control panels. Use WebSearch and WebFetch (load them via ToolSearch first with query "select:WebFetch,WebSearch").

Look at these REAL panels and document what features they actually offer (cite specific URLs you fetched):
1. Pterodactyl Panel (pterodactyl.io, its docs, and its GitHub) — the open-source industry standard
2. Crafty Controller (craftycontrol.com / docs.craftycontrol.com)
3. AMP by CubeCoders (cubecoders.com/AMP)
4. Commercial Minecraft host dashboards: Apex Hosting, Shockbyte, BisectHosting — what their panel feature pages advertise (many use Multicraft or Pterodactyl)
5. Optionally: Multicraft (multicraft.org), the older industry standard

I need a comprehensive, concrete feature checklist of what Minecraft server owners expect from a web dashboard — MINECRAFT-SPECIFIC features, not generic VPS management. Things like: live console with command input, start/stop/restart/kill, file manager, player management (ops/whitelist/bans/kick), world management, backups/scheduled backups, plugin/mod installer, modpack installer, server.properties editor, version/jar switcher, scheduled tasks/cron, subusers & permissions, SFTP access, resource graphs, database (MySQL) provisioning, port/allocation management, etc.

For each feature note which panels have it, so I can distinguish "table stakes" from "nice to have". Report back a structured checklist with source URLs. Be concrete and factual — no generic advice. Under 600 words in your final report.

Pterodactyl is described as "the open-source game server management panel built with PHP, React, and Go." It prioritizes security by running "all game servers in isolated Docker containers."

Research complete. Findings below.

## Minecraft panel feature checklist (P=Pterodactyl, C=Crafty, A=AMP, M=Multicraft, Apex/Shock/Bisect = commercial hosts)

**Table stakes — every panel has it**
| Feature | Panels |
|---|---|
| Live streaming console + command input (websocket) | P, C, A, M, Shockbyte ("real-time console… execute commands instantly", w/ highlighting, filtering, log sharing), Bisect, Apex |
| Start / Stop / Restart / Kill (force) | P, C, A, M, Shockbyte ("start, stop, kill, resync") |
| In-browser file manager (browse/edit/upload/download/archive) | P, C, A, M, all three hosts |
| Backups: manual + scheduled, retention/max-count limits | P (per-server Backups tab w/ retention limits), C (Backup Manager: max backups, shutdown-during-backup, backup location), A, M, Shockbyte, Bisect ("7 days of backups") |
| Scheduled tasks / cron (restarts, commands, backups) | P (cron-syntax scheduler), C, A (can also trigger on in-game events like player join/leave), M, Shockbyte |
| Resource graphs: CPU / RAM / disk / network, live + historical | P, C (+ OpenMetrics/Prometheus export), A, Apex, Bisect, Shockbyte |
| Subusers with granular per-permission access | P (Users tab, per-permission), C (role-based), A, M (multi-level permissions), Bisect (per-permission + "All Permissions"), Shockbyte (custom roles), Apex |
| Config editor for server.properties | C (edit any server file incl. server.properties), A, M, Shockbyte ("Config Manager"), Bisect ("Advanced Config Editor") |
| One-click plugin installer (Spigot/Bukkit browse+install/delete) | A, M ("built-in plugin list"), Apex (Bukget), Shockbyte, Bisect (plugins + datapacks) |
| One-click modpack installer (CurseForge/FTB/Modrinth) | A, Apex (200+), Shockbyte (2000+), Bisect (2,300+ / 700+ jar menu) |
| Version / JAR switcher (Vanilla/Paper/Forge/Fabric + MC version) | A, C, M, all hosts (Pterodactyl does it via Startup tab egg variables) |
| FTP/SFTP access | P (built-in SFTP), M (integrated FTP server), Apex |

**Common but not universal**
| Feature | Panels |
|---|---|
| MySQL database provisioning per server (user-controlled password) | P (Databases tab), M, Apex |
| Player management UI — online list, kick/ban/pardon, op, whitelist | C, A, M ("live chat, player management"), Bisect ("Player Manager"), Shockbyte ("see who's online") — Pterodactyl has **none** (console commands only) |
| Port / IP allocation management | P (Network tab), M |
| Startup parameters / JVM flags / env-var editor | P (Startup tab), A, M |
| Bedrock support alongside Java | C, A, M |
| 2FA / passkeys on panel login | C (TOTP + passkeys), P (2FA) |
| API for automation/billing integration | P, C (API v2), A, M (WHMCS/Blesta/FOSSBilling) |
| Activity/audit log | P (Activity tab) |
| "Instances" — multiple server setups on one plan, one-click swap | A (multi-instance), Shockbyte, Bisect |

**Nice to have / differentiators**
- Public status page + PWA install (Crafty)
- Webhooks (Crafty)
- Event-driven scheduler triggered by in-game events (AMP)
- Console log filtering, syntax highlighting, shareable log links (Shockbyte)
- Theming/plugin extensibility of the panel itself (AMP)
- World management (upload/download/reset/seed) — implicit via file manager everywhere; no panel advertises it as a first-class tab
- Game-switching (change to any of 110+ games) — Bisect

**Notable gap to exploit:** Pterodactyl, the OSS standard most hosts white-label, has **no Minecraft-aware layer at all** — no player list, no ops/whitelist/ban UI, no plugin or modpack installer, no server.properties form editor. Commercial hosts (Apex, Shockbyte, Bisect) win on exactly those. A Minecraft panel that ships Pterodactyl-grade infra plus the MC-specific layer is the differentiated product.
